title: Audit every claim against its own limits and publish the v5 registry
source_handoff: third review round: five verified claim-versus-limit mismatches, plus the sweep they imply
acceptance_criteria: All 29 active claims are audited for the class 'the statement asserts more than its limits, trials or anchors support', not only the five known cases; the audit's findings for every claim are recorded, including the claims that pass unchanged
v2-10's unsupported 'at no measurable cost' is removed; the claim is about refusals, not throughput, in both statement and limits
v2-16's statement keeps only the measured read result; the write-path sentence is removed from the claim and its limits keep saying read throughput only

v2-07 either gains the sibling runs that support its 'stable across three runs' limit as corroborating anchors, or has that limit reworded so it no longer cites repetition the claim's trials do not declare
v2-14's limit is scoped to the 2.2-3.5x range instead of reading as a corpus-wide gap

v3-06 keeps its statement, because the colocated layout's PRIMARY KEY ((person_id) HASH, ...) makes one donor's donations hash to one tablet by configuration; its limits say the logical partition mapping follows from the primary key's hash column while physical tablet/leader placement was not observed
book/evidence/v5/ is a new package; v1-v4 stay frozen and byte-unchanged, no tag moves, and a SUPERSESSION_LEDGER.md records every changed statement, limit or anchor with what it previously said

tools/evidence gains validate-v5, the default validate dispatches v5, and one new mechanical lint: a statement or limit citing a repetition count greater than the declared trials, with no corroborating anchor, fails
The book wiring moves to v5 (build.sh, lib/evidence.typ) with no prose change in this task
validation: go test ./... green including the new lint fixtures
git diff against the v4 tag shows only the intended claims
